s: Which Vijayanagara ruler patronized the Ashtadiggajas?
x:
Sri Krishnadevaraya (1509–1529 CE) was the greatest ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire and is celebrated as one of the greatest patrons of Telugu literature. His royal court was adorned by the Ashtadiggajas (Eight Great Telugu Poets), who produced some of the finest literary works in Telugu. Among them were Allasani Peddana, Nandi Timmana, Dhurjati, Tenali Ramakrishna, Pingali Surana, Ayyalaraju Ramabhadrudu, Madayyagari Mallana and Ramarajabhushanudu. Krishnadevaraya himself was a distinguished scholar and authored the famous Telugu work Amuktamalyada.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

s: Krishna Deva Raya's drama "Jambavati Kalyanam" was written in which language?
x:
Sri Krishnadevaraya was a distinguished scholar proficient in several languages. While his celebrated work Amuktamalyada was written in Telugu, his drama Jambavati Kalyanam, based on the marriage of Lord Krishna and Jambavati, was composed in Sanskrit. This reflects his mastery over both Telugu and Sanskrit literature.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).

s: Krishnadevaraya's Bhuvana Vijaya Bhavan was described in detail by whom?
x:
The Portuguese traveller Domingo Paes visited the Vijayanagara Empire during the reign of Sri Krishnadevaraya. In his travel account, he gave a detailed description of the Bhuvana Vijaya Sabha (Royal Court), the grandeur of the royal palace, festivals, military strength, markets and administrative system. His account remains one of the most authentic contemporary sources for the history of Krishnadevaraya and the Vijayanagara Empire.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

Tirumalamba, a distinguished woman scholar of the Vijayanagara period, authored the Sanskrit work Varadambika Parinayam. The work narrates the marriage of Achyuta Devaraya and Varadambika and is regarded as one of the finest literary compositions by a woman writer during the Vijayanagara age.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: Which of the following does not belong to the subject matter of Amuktamalyada?
o: Tells the story of Godadevi's marriage.
Reveals the genealogy from Bukkaraya to Krishnadevaraya.
x:
Amuktamalyada, written by Sri Krishnadevaraya in Telugu, narrates the story of Andal (Godadevi) and her marriage to Lord Ranganatha. Apart from its devotional theme, the work contains valuable discussions on: • Principles of ideal kingship • Administration and statecraft • Political advice to rulers • Genealogy of the Vijayanagara rulers However, it does not describe Krishnadevaraya's military campaigns or invasions.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).
